core_meaning.primary_meaning: Aleem is an Arabic-origin name meaning “Knowledgeable, all-knowing”.
core_meaning.literal_meaning: The name is the Arabic word itself, used unchanged as a given name rather than a derived or diminutive form.
core_meaning.meaning_explanation: Aleem corresponds to the Arabic form عليم (Arabic root ع ل م (ʿ-l-m); عَلِيم (ʿalīm)). Its core sense is knowledgeable; all-knowing. Aleem is Arabic عَلِيم (ʿalīm) 'Knowledgeable, all-knowing', the faʿīl-pattern adjective of knowledge built on the root ع ل م (ʿ-l-m). Aleem is a variant romanization of Alim.

etymology.morphology: Faʿīl-pattern intensive adjective built on the root ع ل م.
etymology.etymological_meaning: From the root ع ل م (ʿ-l-m)
etymology.etymology_explanation: The form عليم is an established Arabic lexical item — the faʿīl-pattern adjective of the root ع ل م — and Aleem is the word itself used as a personal name rather than a derived or diminutive form.
etymology.false_etymology_warning: No derivation beyond the documented Arabic form is asserted. Any etymology that attributes this spelling to a different root or language without a source should be treated as unverified.

language_notes.primary: Arabic is the language of the recorded form عليم.
language_notes.usage: Other scripts are transliterations of the name into those writing systems; they are not independent origins.

origin.origin_explanation: The name originates in Arabic and circulates in Muslim naming through established multilingual use.

religion.religious_status: Culturally used; not inherently a doctrinal term
religion.religious_explanation: Aleem is used by Muslims as a personal name, but the word itself is lexical in origin; its Islamic association is cultural rather than scriptural.

quranic_status.note: Aleem is not independently established as a Qur'anic personal name, so no Qur'anic basis is claimed.

islamic_naming_context.context: Muslim naming culture in South Asia and the Persianate world
islamic_naming_context.interpretation: Its lexical sense is a positive quality that families may wish for a child.
islamic_naming_context.important_distinction: Muslim use of the name is not evidence that the word is Qur'anic or religiously prescribed.

cultural_context.personal_name_interpretation: As a personal name it can be read as a wish for the quality it names.
